AS OF ISSUE #2593 EVERY WALKED SURFACE HOLDS axeSerious 0 / axeCritical 0 — those two are no longer debt lines anywhere, so a nonzero reading is a regression, not a carried defect. The one surface that could not hold it as written is `/admin/design-system`, whose job includes SHOWING what a failing token looks like: its three deliberate specimens carry `data-axe-exempt="<why>"`, the lane excludes those subtrees and prints `exempt<n>` on the surface's line of every run, and `scripts/__tests__/axe-exemption-scope.test.ts` fails if the attribute appears anywhere but that page. An exemption is a named node in a reviewable diff; a nonzero budget row is a number nobody can attribute. Where a surface breaks one of the REMAINING floors today; where a surface breaks one of those TODAY the entry keeps the measured value and carries a `knownDebt` note naming the defect, printed under every run. A slice that fixes a surface lowers its ceilings in the same PR. A surface nobody can walk yet is `{"status":"unwalked","reason":…}` — listed in the output and in the coverage line, never silently green. Issue #2582 (PR #2619) moved the probe's `occ`/`reachable` boundary, and it moved it in BOTH directions. A control is `occ` when the centre of its VISIBLE INTERSECTION with (viewport n its own SCROLL PORT) hit-tests to something else, and `reachable` when that intersection is EMPTY but a gesture can bring it back — see `probe.js`'s `scrollPort` / `probe`. The old rule tested the element's raw centre against the bare viewport. LOOSER than the old rule: a control lying wholly outside its port's box (the deck-builder's off-strip `Delete column MV n` buttons) is no longer `occ`, and neither is one straddling a port's clip edge with a band below it (the lobby's `Your Events (all)` under the new bottom nav) — `<main>` paints nothing there, so nothing can be occluding it. STRICTER than the old rule: a control PARTLY clipped by its port is now hit-tested over the strip it still paints, where a raw centre would have been thrown away as out-of-window (`design-system-dialog`'s section-08 Cancel/Confirm specimens), and a `position: fixed` box gets no port at all rather than borrowing an ancestor scroller's rectangle. Rows not re-recorded still measure below their number and are deliberately left alone: those readings vary with the deployment's own deck/pool data, and the notes on them describe debt the surface's own slice owns. Issue #2658 adds `small`: count of visible in-band interactive controls under 44px on their smaller dimension (`probe.js`'s `smallN`). This key is DELIBERATELY POINTER-BLIND — the probe applies the same 44px test at every viewport, but `--control-h` resolves to 32px under `pointer: fine` ON PURPOSE (`src/index.css:942,946-948`, citing WCAG 2.5.8, a TOUCH-target rule). Every nonzero `small` ceiling below carries a `knownDebt` note saying explicitly which of the two it is — a reader must never "fix" a desktop reading by shrinking a touch target, or dismiss a touch reading as "just the desktop thing".
